blocks.x: Master Data, Governance & Cataloging, shipped on a signed baseline: the scope we take, the weekly delivery rhythm, the platform rails underneath, and the delta we commit to at every gate.

Every intelligence program inherits the estate's master data sins: duplicate customers, orphan products, supplier records with three tax IDs. We run MDM programs that establish golden records with survivorship rules, stewardship workflows and source-system feedback — for customer, product, supplier, location and employee domains — integrated with the catalog so every dataset references governed entities rather than local interpretations.

Cataloging makes the estate legible: automated metadata harvesting, business glossary curation, classification tags driving access control, and a data product registry with owners and SLAs. Privacy obligations (GDPR/CCPA) become executable: subject data maps, retention policies and DSAR automation tied to the same tags. Governance turns from committee theater into system behavior.

The cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability, and it does not flex by account. The first quarter of the rhythm is verification: weeks 1–2 measure the current metric with your team and lock it by signature. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with your control owner receiving evidence weekly. Weeks 9–12 industrialize: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and the measured delta against the signed baseline. Gates are binding: miss one and the program stops or redirects with a documented decision.
